source.publisher: Ballymoney Free Press and Northern Counties Advertiser (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: four nominations for nine seats, no contest; the five unfilled seats are recorded by the 9-seat contest.

note: Triennial election of the Limavady Urban District Council, nominations 12 January 1926; only four nominations for nine seats, so there was no contest (Ballymoney Free Press and Northern Counties Advertiser, 14 January 1926, p. 2). The paper names the nine retiring councillors and reports that only four nominations were received, for Robert Douglas, Douglas Boyd, Thomas Ferris (old members) and James Wray (new). 'No contest, of course, will take place, and it will be necessary to select members to fill the remaining five vacancies.' The five men later selected are not named in this report; the annual meeting report of 26 January shows M. M. M'Causland, William Arthur, William Hunt and F. J. Coghlan still active, but does not state how their seats were filled. No party label was printed. Returned unopposed.
